planned_source_categories.why_relevant: WHO AFRO, WHO HQ Disease Outbreak News, Africa CDC, DRC Ministry of Health (Ministère de la Santé Publique, Hygiène et Prévention), and INRB (Institut National de Recherche Biomédicale) are the authoritative primary reporting agencies for DRC Mpox. These sources publish weekly and monthly epidemiological bulletins with subnational (province, health zone) case and death breakdowns, confirmed/probable/suspected case classifications, and clade I/Ib distinctions directly relevant to the August 2024 target window.

WHO global Mpox situation reports, ECDC rapid risk assessments, OCHA humanitarian situation reports, and Reliefweb updates provide independently compiled DRC Mpox data for August 2024. These serve as validation sources because they aggregate data from official DRC sources but are published independently, enabling cross-check of case and death counts.

Peer-reviewed studies and preprints (PubMed, medRxiv, Lancet, NEJM, Eurosurveillance) on DRC Mpox clade I/Ib epidemiology published in 2024 provide case definitions, surveillance methodology context, and may contain extractable case/death data for the August 2024 period. Essential for interpreting count semantics and normalizing confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected classifications.

Structured public-health databases including Global.health line lists, Our World in Data Mpox tracker, WHO Mpox data repository, and ProMED archive provide machine-readable or structured DRC Mpox counts for August 2024. These are held back for validation to cross-check extracted records from primary collection sources.

Reputable news outlets (Reuters, AP, AFP, BBC), humanitarian portals (Reliefweb, OCHA), and health news aggregators (CIDRAP, Health Policy Watch) published DRC Mpox outbreak coverage in August 2024 coinciding with the WHO PHEIC declaration. These sources provide early outbreak signals, subnational location corroboration, and may cite official figures directly quotable as evidence.

selection_manifest.human_review_reason: The ECDC is a highly authoritative international public health body (authority_score=0.95), and this report is directly disease-relevant (disease_relevance_score=0.95) and timely (timeliness_score=0.95) for the August 2024 Mpox/clade I window. However, the deterministic model correctly penalizes this source on local and geographic granularity grounds (local_relevance_score=0.58; geographic_granularity_score=0.58): ECDC epidemiological updates on DRC Mpox are produced from a European surveillance perspective and typically aggregate or summarize DRC data rather than originating it. The source is therefore best suited to a 'context' role rather than primary 'collection'. The role_hint was 'collection' but both the deterministic role assignment and the source_role_final converge on 'context', and the 'screening_and_critic_disagree' risk flag warrants LLM advisory attention. The data_granularity_score of 0.68 and machine_readability_score of 0.72 suggest the document may contain useful numeric summaries but is unlikely to provide the subnational (province/health-zone) granularity required by the collection spec. The independence_score of 0.90 is strong, indicating ECDC is not simply republishing DRC MoH verbatim, but this also means ECDC figures may diverge from primary DRC sources and introduce double-counting risk if used alongside WHO, Africa CDC, or INRB reports. The risk_penalty of 0.10 is modest but appropriate. Overall, this source is credible for contextual validation and cross-referencing but should not be the primary extraction source for DRC subnational case/death counts.

This source is a Facebook post from the account "cgtnafrica" — a social media page, not an official public health agency, international organization, or structured database. Despite the deterministic assessment assigning an authority_score of 0.88 (likely inflated by the CGTN Africa brand recognition) and a source_type label of "international_organization_report," the actual hosting domain is facebook.com, which is a social media platform with no editorial controls, no structured data, no versioning, and no verifiable provenance chain for epidemiological figures. The source_type label "international_organization_report" is a critical metadata mislabel — CGTN Africa is a state-affiliated broadcast media outlet, not an international public health organization. The post appears to be a media summary or repost of health official statements, not a primary or authoritative epidemiological report. Key structural deficiencies include: (1) no publisher metadata, (2) no snippet available for content verification, (3) social media platform with no data integrity guarantees, (4) low local_relevance_score (0.25) and low geographic_granularity_score (0.3), indicating the source likely lacks subnational or health-zone-level data required by the collection spec, (5) the query used targeted authoritative domains (who.int, africacdc.org, reliefweb.int) but this result resolved to facebook.com — a strong signal of query-result domain mismatch. The risk_penalty of 0.16 and the "screening_and_critic_disagree" flag further indicate internal inconsistency in the deterministic pipeline. The source should not be used as a primary or validation data source for structured epidemiological extraction. If any numeric claims are present in the post, they must be traced back to and verified against the original official source (e.g., DRC MoH, WHO, Africa CDC) before any data ingestion. Human review is recommended to adjudicate the source_type mislabel and confirm exclusion or downgrade.

This source is a Facebook post from Arise TV News — a broadcast media outlet — sharing what appears to be a summary of WHO-reported Mpox statistics for DRC in 2024. Several compounding credibility concerns apply:

1. **Domain mismatch vs. source_type**: The domain is `facebook.com` (a social media platform), but the source_type is tagged as `international_organization_report`. This is a significant metadata misclassification. The content may reference WHO data, but the source itself is a social media post by a news broadcaster, not an official WHO publication. This mismatch alone warrants a credibility downgrade and role reassignment.

2. **Secondary/tertiary provenance**: Even if Arise TV News accurately relays WHO figures, this is at minimum a second-hand report. The original WHO situation report or Disease Outbreak Notice (DON) is the authoritative source and should be sought directly. Using this Facebook post as a collection source risks introducing transcription errors, truncation, or loss of methodological context.

3. **Data granularity limitations**: The snippet references national-level aggregates (≥8,000 cases, 384 deaths for all of 2024). The collection task requires subnational granularity (province- and health-zone-level) for August 2024 specifically. A Facebook post headline is extremely unlikely to contain the required `subnational_location`, `locality`, `cases_confirmed`, `cases_probable`, `cases_suspected`, or `hospitalizations` fields at the needed resolution.

4. **Missing publisher field**: The publisher is null, which is anomalous even for a social media post — the page owner (Arise TV News) should be resolvable. This may indicate incomplete metadata harvesting.

5. **Temporal scope mismatch**: The figures cited (≥8,000 cases, 384 deaths) appear to be cumulative 2024 totals, not August 2024 monthly data. This does not align with the collection window of 2024-08-01 to 2024-08-31.

6. **`screening_and_critic_disagree` flag**: The deterministic assessment itself flags internal disagreement, which is a signal that this source warrants additional scrutiny before any role is finalized.

7. **PHEIC context risk**: During the August 2024 PHEIC declaration period, social media posts referencing WHO data are especially prone to selective quoting, outdated figures, or conflation of cumulative vs. period-specific counts.

**Advisory recommendation**: Downgrade role from `context` to `deprioritized` or `discard` for direct data collection purposes. The primary WHO source (WHO DON, WHO AFRO sitrep, or INRB bulletin) should be retrieved directly. This Facebook post may serve only as a breadcrumb to locate the original WHO report, not as a citable data source.

Recent global updates for mpox can also be found in the WHO mpox surveillance report. WHO conducted the latest global mpox rapid risk assessment in early August 2024. Based on information available at the time, the mpox risk was assessed as follows: • In the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and neighbouring countries: high. • In areas of the Democratic Republic of the Congo where mpox is endemic: high. • In Nigeria and other countries of West, Central and East Africa where mpox is endemic: moderate. • In all other countries in Africa and around the world: moderate (while in individual countries or regional bloc assessments may vary, and the risk may be assessed as low). Individual-level risk is largely dependent on individual factors such as exposure risk and immune status, regardless of geographic area, epidemiological context, biological sex, gender identity or sexual orientation. This situation update in Africa presents reported confirmed mpox cases and deaths,2 as described in the WHO case definitions published in the Surveillance, case investigation and contact tracing for mpox interim guidance. It also presents nationally reported suspected mpox cases, as defined by the countries that have reported them, to provide the reader with more information on epidemiological trends in countries with limitations in access to testing, such as the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Note: The indicator of suspected cases should be interpreted with caution, as these are recorded according to varying national case definitions, and in some countries, suspected cases that undergo testing are not removed from the overall count of suspected cases, regardless of whether the test result is positive (confirmed case) or negative (discarded case). In the absence of more detailed information, it is currently not possible to correctly subtract confirmed cases from the total number of suspected cases reported; therefore, the confirmed cases represent a subset of suspected cases. Definitions of suspected mpox cases for the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Burundi can be found here. 2 For the WHO European region, both confirmed and probable cases are included within confirmed case counts and detailed case data. Mpox: Multi-country External Situation Report n.38 9 Global operational updates The WHO health emergency prevention, preparedness, response and resilience (HEPR) framework underpins both the Strategic Framework for enhancing prevention and control of mpox (2024-2027) and the current emergency response to the mpox Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC). Aligned with the HEPR framework, the WHO Global Strategic Preparedness and Response Plan (SPRP) for mpox focuses on strengthening five core components—the 5Cs: 1. Emergency coordination: Efficient coordination for timely crisis response. 2. Collaborative surveillance: Real-time data integration for early threat detection. 3. Community protection: Engaging communities in prevention and resilience-building measures. 4. Safe and scalable care: Equipping health systems to provide essential care with scalable capacity. 5. Access to and delivery of countermeasures: Ensuring equitable distribution of medical countermeasures. This section provides updates on the WHO global mpox response as of 22 September 2024. 1. Emergency coordination • Through its Country Offices WHO is supporting Member States in operationalizing response plan guided by the Strategic Preparedness and Response Plan (SPRP). Coordinating with Partners WHO is supporting national coordination structures including activated Incident Management Systems (IMS) in technical areas such as surveillance and epidemiological analysis, vaccination, infection prevention and control (IPC), risk communication and community engagement (RCCE), treatment and therapeutics, operation support and logistics (OSL), among others. On request of Member States, WHO AFRO Regional Office and headquarters have deployed experts to support response operations. • WHO is still working with relevant partners to design research activities for a better understanding of the outbreak and evidence-based strategies (refer to special focus below). 2. Collaborative surveillance • Epidemiological data on mpox updated weekly can be accessed on the WHO surveillance report here. • WHO updated the template transmission studies protocol to support mpox field investigations. • A webinar on the use of digital and analytics tools for mpox response was held on 24 September 2024. Countries shared their experience using Go.Data for mpox response. Analytical tools and initiatives highlighted included the Collaboratory epidemiological parameters for modelling and analysis, and software tools for addressing common analytics tasks. • An EPI-WIN webinar on collaborative surveillance for mpox was held on 26 September 2024. WHO and Africa Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) shared updates on current mpox global surveillance, the main activities to support countries with mpox surveillance, persisting challenges and an update of the current epidemiological situation. • WHO convened the Orthopoxvirus Laboratory Network to review and update interim guidance on diagnostic testing for monkeypox virus (MPXV). The upcoming update to this interim guidance shall include the latest guidance on MPXV near-point-of-care tests and antigen rapid diagnostic tests. • WHO and partners initiated the diagnostics workstream of the Access and Allocation Mechanism (AAM). 3. Community protection • Coordination for community protection continues, covering risk communication, RCCE and infodemic management; community IPC; water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH); home-based care; vaccination; border health and mass gatherings; and managing risks of transmission between animals and humans. Mpox: Multi-country External Situation Report n.38 10 Key multi-partner and civil society engagement and advocacy meetings were held in the reporting period: • The Community Protection Partners Network meeting held on 20 September 2024 focused on home-based care and community-based infection prevention and control, especially for low resource settings. • The informal community reference group of civil society organizations, networks and researchers was held on 20 September with representatives from 15 Countries from WHO AFRO, EURO and PAHO regions. Community representatives emphasized the importance of 1) ensuring that messages reach key populations, especially communities affected by HIV, and 2) community preparedness and involvement in the response to address complex layers of stigma and discrimination which hamper efforts to reach key populations and other marginalized groups. Special efforts are required to reach people with disabilities. • The Collective Service is an interagency initiative between IFRC, UNICEF, WHO, and GOARN for the coordinated delivery of RCCE for public health emergencies. A bi-monthly global call provides a platform for partners to share and hear updates on the global situation. 4. Safe and scalable care • A rapid assessment tool for IPC and WASH in health facilities has been shared with the African Regional Office and affected countries. This is being implemented in many health facilities in hotspot areas to identify opportunities for improvement in IPC practices and WASH services to ensure health workers and patients remain safe while receiving care. • Posters for health and care workers for putting on and removing PPE for mpox are available on the WHO website. Over 2500 participants from affected countries and around the world— scientists, Member State representatives, public health professionals, funding agencies and private sector representatives— gathered to accelerate development of innovations to control the mpox epidemic. The meeting aimed to develop an emergency mpox research response agenda, enhance collaboration and partnerships, and outline key steps and timelines for addressing research gaps, emphasizing the leading role of affected countries and their researchers in shaping the research agenda. Key principles guiding the meeting included collaboration, leadership from affected regions, alignment with outbreak response goals, and a people-centered focus. There was consensus on the need for studies that 1) contribute to controlling the outbreak; 2) guide interventions so that those at the highest risk of infection are protected, promptly diagnosed, and receive optimal care; and 3) catalyze integration of research in each area of outbreak response, in a collaborative manner and with researchers and ministries of health of the affected countries in the driving seat. Evaluate and deploy new rapid and sensitive diagnostic tests that detect all monkeypox virus (MPXV) clades and help with the differential diagnosis of diseases that can resemble mpox. 3. Define and implement all elements of an optimized clinical standard of care for all mpox patients. 4. Promote development of new therapeutics and evaluation of safety and efficacy of prioritized candidate therapeutics for mpox, in coordinated collaborative multicenter trials. 5. Conduct research on animal models and use animal models towards the determination of correlates of protection, and support research on immunoassays. 6. Define regulatory pathways for “next generation” medical countermeasures. 7. Facilitate availability of vaccines in areas with sustained human to human transmission as part of an integrated response, and promote generation of critical data regarding vaccine safety, performance and delivery strategies. 8. Use existing tools to incorporate Good Participatory Practices and community engagement in research including public health research. 9. Integrate research into outbreak response activities. 10. Embrace and expand opportunities for coordination and collaboration of all research initiatives with local authorities and research institutions, with researchers from affected countries and ministries of health at the centre of the response. Aligned with the HEPR framework, the WHO Global Strategic Preparedness and Response Plan (SPRP) for mpox focuses on strengthening five core components—the 5Cs: 1. Emergency coordination: Efficient coordination for timely crisis response. 2. Collaborative surveillance: Real-time data integration for early threat detection. 3. Community protection: Engaging communities in prevention and resilience-building measures. 4. Safe and scalable care: Equipping health systems to provide essential care with scalable capacity. 5. On request of Member States, WHO AFRO Regional Office and headquarters have deployed experts to support response operations. • WHO is still working with relevant partners to design research activities for a better understanding of the outbreak and evidence-based strategies (refer to special focus below). 2. Community protection • Coordination for community protection continues, covering risk communication, RCCE and infodemic management; community IPC; water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH); home-based care; vaccination; border health and mass gatherings; and managing risks of transmission between animals and humans. In a comprehensive effort to synchronize research initiatives with the immediate requirements of mpox outbreak management, discussions emphasized collaboration, regulatory and ethics considerations, and national leadership. Over 2500 participants from affected countries and around the world— scientists, Member State representatives, public health professionals, funding agencies and private sector representatives— gathered to accelerate development of innovations to control the mpox epidemic. The meeting aimed to develop an emergency mpox research response agenda, enhance collaboration and partnerships, and outline key steps and timelines for addressing research gaps, emphasizing the leading role of affected countries and their researchers in shaping the research agenda. Key principles guiding the meeting included collaboration, leadership from affected regions, alignment with outbreak response goals, and a people-centered focus. There was consensus on the need for studies that 1) contribute to controlling the outbreak; 2) guide interventions so that those at the highest risk of infection are protected, promptly diagnosed, and receive optimal care; and 3) catalyze integration of research in each area of outbreak response, in a collaborative manner and with researchers and ministries of health of the affected countries in the driving seat. Ten immediate next steps for a coordinated Research Roadmap: 1. Obtain additional data on mpox transmission and epidemiology, including clinical outcomes and risk factors for severe disease. 2. Evaluate and deploy new rapid and sensitive diagnostic tests that detect all monkeypox virus (MPXV) clades and help with the differential diagnosis of diseases that can resemble mpox. 3. Define and implement all elements of an optimized clinical standard of care for all mpox patients. 4. Promote development of new therapeutics and evaluation of safety and efficacy of prioritized candidate therapeutics for mpox, in coordinated collaborative multicenter trials. 5. Conduct research on animal models and use animal models towards the determination of correlates of protection, and support research on immunoassays. 6. Define regulatory pathways for “next generation” medical countermeasures. 7. Facilitate availability of vaccines in areas with sustained human to human transmission as part of an integrated response, and promote generation of critical data regarding vaccine safety, performance and delivery strategies. 8. Use existing tools to incorporate Good Participatory Practices and community engagement in research including public health research. 9. Integrate research into outbreak response activities. 10. Embrace and expand opportunities for coordination and collaboration of all research initiatives with local authorities and research institutions, with researchers from affected countries and ministries of health at the centre of the response. A summary of these immediate next steps can be found here. A full research roadmap will follow. Mpox: Multi-country External Situation Report n.38 9 Global operational updates The WHO health emergency prevention, preparedness, response and resilience (HEPR) framework underpins both the Strategic Framework for enhancing prevention and control of mpox (2024-2027) and the current emergency response to the mpox Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC). Aligned with the HEPR framework, the WHO Global Strategic Preparedness and Response Plan (SPRP) for mpox focuses on strengthening five core components—the 5Cs: 1. Emergency coordination: Efficient coordination for timely crisis response. 2. Collaborative surveillance: Real-time data integration for early threat detection. 3. Community protection: Engaging communities in prevention and resilience-building measures. 4. Safe and scalable care: Equipping health systems to provide essential care with scalable capacity. 5. Access to and delivery of countermeasures: Ensuring equitable distribution of medical countermeasures. This section provides updates on the WHO global mpox response as of 22 September 2024. 1. Emergency coordination • Through its Country Offices WHO is supporting Member States in operationalizing response plan guided by the Strategic Preparedness and Response Plan (SPRP). On request of Member States, WHO AFRO Regional Office and headquarters have deployed experts to support response operations. • WHO is still working with relevant partners to design research activities for a better understanding of the outbreak and evidence-based strategies (refer to special focus below). 2. Community protection • Coordination for community protection continues, covering risk communication, RCCE and infodemic management; community IPC; water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH); home-based care; vaccination; border health and mass gatherings; and managing risks of transmission between animals and humans. In a comprehensive effort to synchronize research initiatives with the immediate requirements of mpox outbreak management, discussions emphasized collaboration, regulatory and ethics considerations, and national leadership. Over 2500 participants from affected countries and around the world— scientists, Member State representatives, public health professionals, funding agencies and private sector representatives— gathered to accelerate development of innovations to control the mpox epidemic. The meeting aimed to develop an emergency mpox research response agenda, enhance collaboration and partnerships, and outline key steps and timelines for addressing research gaps, emphasizing the leading role of affected countries and their researchers in shaping the research agenda. Key principles guiding the meeting included collaboration, leadership from affected regions, alignment with outbreak response goals, and a people-centered focus. There was consensus on the need for studies that 1) contribute to controlling the outbreak; 2) guide interventions so that those at the highest risk of infection are protected, promptly diagnosed, and receive optimal care; and 3) catalyze integration of research in each area of outbreak response, in a collaborative manner and with researchers and ministries of health of the affected countries in the driving seat. Ten immediate next steps for a coordinated Research Roadmap: 1. Obtain additional data on mpox transmission and epidemiology, including clinical outcomes and risk factors for severe disease. 2. Evaluate and deploy new rapid and sensitive diagnostic tests that detect all monkeypox virus (MPXV) clades and help with the differential diagnosis of diseases that can resemble mpox. 3. Define and implement all elements of an optimized clinical standard of care for all mpox patients. 4. Promote development of new therapeutics and evaluation of safety and efficacy of prioritized candidate therapeutics for mpox, in coordinated collaborative multicenter trials. 5. Conduct research on animal models and use animal models towards the determination of correlates of protection, and support research on immunoassays. 6. Define regulatory pathways for “next generation” medical countermeasures. 7. Facilitate availability of vaccines in areas with sustained human to human transmission as part of an integrated response, and promote generation of critical data regarding vaccine safety, performance and delivery strategies. 8. Use existing tools to incorporate Good Participatory Practices and community engagement in research including public health research. 9. Integrate research into outbreak response activities. 10. Embrace and expand opportunities for coordination and collaboration of all research initiatives with local authorities and research institutions, with researchers from affected countries and ministries of health at the centre of the response. A summary of these immediate next steps can be found here. A full research roadmap will follow. Mpox: Multi-country External Situation Report n.38 9 Global operational updates The WHO health emergency prevention, preparedness, response and resilience (HEPR) framework underpins both the Strategic Framework for enhancing prevention and control of mpox (2024-2027) and the current emergency response to the mpox Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC). Aligned with the HEPR framework, the WHO Global Strategic Preparedness and Response Plan (SPRP) for mpox focuses on strengthening five core components—the 5Cs: 1. Emergency coordination: Efficient coordination for timely crisis response. 2. Collaborative surveillance: Real-time data integration for early threat detection. 3. Community protection: Engaging communities in prevention and resilience-building measures. 4. Safe and scalable care: Equipping health systems to provide essential care with scalable capacity. 5. Access to and delivery of countermeasures: Ensuring equitable distribution of medical countermeasures. This section provides updates on the WHO global mpox response as of 22 September 2024. 1. Emergency coordination • Through its Country Offices WHO is supporting Member States in operationalizing response plan guided by the Strategic Preparedness and Response Plan (SPRP). On request of Member States, WHO AFRO Regional Office and headquarters have deployed experts to support response operations. • WHO is still working with relevant partners to design research activities for a better understanding of the outbreak and evidence-based strategies (refer to special focus below). 2. Collaborative surveillance • Epidemiological data on mpox updated weekly can be accessed on the WHO surveillance report here. • WHO updated the template transmission studies protocol to support mpox field investigations. • A webinar on the use of digital and analytics tools for mpox response was held on 24 September 2024. Countries shared their experience using Go.Data for mpox response. Analytical tools and initiatives highlighted included the Collaboratory epidemiological parameters for modelling and analysis, and software tools for addressing common analytics tasks. • An EPI-WIN webinar on collaborative surveillance for mpox was held on 26 September 2024. WHO and Africa Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) shared updates on current mpox global surveillance, the main activities to support countries with mpox surveillance, persisting challenges and an update of the current epidemiological situation. • WHO convened the Orthopoxvirus Laboratory Network to review and update interim guidance on diagnostic testing for monkeypox virus (MPXV). The upcoming update to this interim guidance shall include the latest guidance on MPXV near-point-of-care tests and antigen rapid diagnostic tests. • WHO and partners initiated the diagnostics workstream of the Access and Allocation Mechanism (AAM). 3. Community protection • Coordination for community protection continues, covering risk communication, RCCE and infodemic management; community IPC; water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH); home-based care; vaccination; border health and mass gatherings; and managing risks of transmission between animals and humans. Mpox: Multi-country External Situation Report n.38 10 Key multi-partner and civil society engagement and advocacy meetings were held in the reporting period: • The Community Protection Partners Network meeting held on 20 September 2024 focused on home-based care and community-based infection prevention and control, especially for low resource settings. • The informal community reference group of civil society organizations, networks and researchers was held on 20 September with representatives from 15 Countries from WHO AFRO, EURO and PAHO regions. Community representatives emphasized the importance of 1) ensuring that messages reach key populations, especially communities affected by HIV, and 2) community preparedness and involvement in the response to address complex layers of stigma and discrimination which hamper efforts to reach key populations and other marginalized groups. Special efforts are required to reach people with disabilities. • The Collective Service is an interagency initiative between IFRC, UNICEF, WHO, and GOARN for the coordinated delivery of RCCE for public health emergencies. A bi-monthly global call provides a platform for partners to share and hear updates on the global situation. 4. Safe and scalable care • A rapid assessment tool for IPC and WASH in health facilities has been shared with the African Regional Office and affected countries. This is being implemented in many health facilities in hotspot areas to identify opportunities for improvement in IPC practices and WASH services to ensure health workers and patients remain safe while receiving care. • Posters for health and care workers for putting on and removing PPE for mpox are available on the WHO website. Steps to put on PPE for mpox, Steps to remove PPE for mpox. 5. Access to and delivery of countermeasures Vaccines • On 19 September 2024, the European Medicines Agency recommended extending the indication of Modified vaccinia Ankara-Bavarian Nordic (MVA-BN) smallpox/mpox vaccine to include adolescents 12 to 17 years of age. • The WHO Global Advisory Committee on Vaccine Safety met on 20 September to review available safety data on mpox vaccines and WHO protocols for safety monitoring. Diagnostics • In working towards emergency use listing of mpox diagnostics EUL, WHO is conducting a bridged assessment of 2 dossiers and expecting another dossier submission in coming days. • On 25 September 2024, WHO met with representatives from Ghana, Nigeria, Rwanda and Tanzania to explore coordination on vaccine safety surveillance data and sharing of data. Mpox: Multi-country External Situation Report n.38 11 Special focus A coordinated research roadmap for monkeypox virus: Immediate research next steps to contribute to control the outbreak From 29-30 August, 2024, the Africa CDC, the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (CEPI), the United States National Institutes of Health (US NIH) and WHO held a scientific conference aimed at aligning research efforts with the practical needs of mpox outbreak control. In a comprehensive effort to synchronize research initiatives with the immediate requirements of mpox outbreak management, discussions emphasized collaboration, regulatory and ethics considerations, and national leadership. Over 2500 participants from affected countries and around the world— scientists, Member State representatives, public health professionals, funding agencies and private sector representatives— gathered to accelerate development of innovations to control the mpox epidemic. The meeting aimed to develop an emergency mpox research response agenda, enhance collaboration and partnerships, and outline key steps and timelines for addressing research gaps, emphasizing the leading role of affected countries and their researchers in shaping the research agenda. Key principles guiding the meeting included collaboration, leadership from affected regions, alignment with outbreak response goals, and a people-centered focus. There was consensus on the need for studies that 1) contribute to controlling the outbreak; 2) guide interventions so that those at the highest risk of infection are protected, promptly diagnosed, and receive optimal care; and 3) catalyze integration of research in each area of outbreak response, in a collaborative manner and with researchers and ministries of health of the affected countries in the driving seat. Ten immediate next steps for a coordinated Research Roadmap: 1. Obtain additional data on mpox transmission and epidemiology, including clinical outcomes and risk factors for severe disease. 2. Evaluate and deploy new rapid and sensitive diagnostic tests that detect all monkeypox virus (MPXV) clades and help with the differential diagnosis of diseases that can resemble mpox. 3. Define and implement all elements of an optimized clinical standard of care for all mpox patients. 4. Promote development of new therapeutics and evaluation of safety and efficacy of prioritized candidate therapeutics for mpox, in coordinated collaborative multicenter trials. 5. Conduct research on animal models and use animal models towards the determination of correlates of protection, and support research on immunoassays. 6. Define regulatory pathways for “next generation” medical countermeasures. 7. Facilitate availability of vaccines in areas with sustained human to human transmission as part of an integrated response, and promote generation of critical data regarding vaccine safety, performance and delivery strategies. 8. Use existing tools to incorporate Good Participatory Practices and community engagement in research including public health research. 9. Integrate research into outbreak response activities. 10. Embrace and expand opportunities for coordination and collaboration of all research initiatives with local authorities and research institutions, with researchers from affected countries and ministries of health at the centre of the response. A summary of these immediate next steps can be found here. A full research roadmap will follow. metric_row_extraction_audit.row_quote: ## Content Search Informing humanitarians worldwide 24/7 — a service provided by UN OCHA [DR Congo](/country/cod) + 14 more # Multi-country outbreak of mpox, External situation report #42 - 9 November 2024 Format : Situation Report Source : * [WHO](/organization/who) Posted Originally published Origin : [View original](https://www.who.int/publications/m/item/multi-country-outbreak-of-mpox--external-situation-report--42--9-november-2024) ## Attachments * [![Preview of 20241109_mpox_external-sitrep_-42.pdf](/sites/default/files/styles/small/public/previews/f6/23/f6238fd2-5642-432e-a66f-09905adce059.png?2584935-1-0) **Download Report** (PDF | 1.2 MB)](/attachments/f6238fd2-5642-432e-a66f-09905adce059/20241109_mpox_external-sitrep_-42.pdf) **Highlights** • Since the last situation report, three additional countries have confirmed travel-related cases of clade Ib MPXV: the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, Zambia and Zimbabwe. • For the first time, local transmission of clade Ib MPXV was reported outside of Africa, in the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, where three (all) household members of the initial case (who had travelled to affected East African countries with clade Ib) were confirmed to have mpox. • The number of mpox cases in Africa shows a general rising trend, driven mainly by cases reported from the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Burundi, and Uganda. • As of 3 November 2024, Clade Ib monkeypox virus (MPXV) has been detected in six provinces in the Democratic Republic of the Congo: South Kivu, North Kivu, Kinshasa, Kasai, Tshopo and Tanganyika, with no new areas known to be affected since the last update. Additionally, 11 other countries have also reported clade Ib MPXV cases.

metric_row_extraction_audit.row_quote: Mpox: Multi-country External Situation Report no.57 1 Mpox Multi-country external situation report no. 57 published 28 August 2025 KEY FIGURES Area Number of reported confirmed cases Number of deaths among confirmed cases Number of reporting countries Global (1 Jan – 31 July 2025)* 34 386 138 84 Key countries (1 Jan – 17 August 2025) Democratic Republic of the Congo 15 377 30 - Uganda 6522 35 - Sierra Leone 5149 52 - Burundi 1394 0 - * Most recent global surveillance data available. Highlights • All clades of monkeypox virus (MPXV) continue to circulate in several countries. When mpox outbreaks are not rapidly contained and human-to-human transmission is not interrupted, they continue to pose a risk of sustained community transmission. Since the last edition of this report, one country, Senegal, has reported mpox for the first time. Efforts to identify the clade are underway. • Furthermore, Türkiye has reported cases of mpox due to clade Ib MPXV for the first time and the Democratic Republic of Congo has reported its first cases of mpox due to clade IIb MPXV. • In July 2025, 47 countries in five (out of six) WHO regions reported a total of 3924 confirmed cases, including 30 deaths (case fatality ratio [CFR] 0.8%). The South-East Asian and Western Pacific regions reported an increase in cases in July 2025, while the African Region, European Region and the Region of the Americas reported a decrease. The Eastern Mediterranean Region did not report any mpox case in July 2025. • Twenty-one countries in Africa have reported ongoing mpox transmission in the past six weeks. Clade IIb MPXV continues to be reported in West Africa, while Central African countries report both clade Ia and clade Ib MPXV, and East African countries report clade Ib MPXV.
